MK: Muscle aches – due to simvastatin-related problems The patient is taking simvastatin 20 mg (generic Zocor) tablets plus simvastatin 40 mg (as an ingredient in the Vytorin drug samples that she was given). The therapeutic duplication of simvastatin is contributing to the muscle aches. Serum concentrations of simvastatin can also be increased by proton pump inhibitors (the patient is also taking omeprazole).

Ecchymoses – due to warfarin-related drug interactions The patient’s warfarin dose was recently changed. The case does not give enough information to know if the dose was recently increased or decreased. Nonetheless, the patient has been concurrently taking a number of medications that can increase the risk of bleeding when used in combination with warfarin including: aspirin (anti-platelet effects), omeprazole (inhibits CYP2C19 which is involved in warfarin metabolism), the recent addition of Lovaza samples (prolongs INR), and the recent addition of a greater simvastatin dose than intended (INR may increase after initiating therapy with a statin) due to therapeutic duplication between simvastatin tablets and the Vytorin samples.
SBP: Poor communication between physicians a. The eye doctor had prescribed latanoprost, but this was not in the patient’s record at the primary care provider’s office. b. The coagulation clinic was not communicating changes in the patient’s warfarin dose to the primary care provider in a timely manner.

Multiple pharmacies and a lack of documentation for over-the-counter/dietary supplement medications Alendronate was called in to a “new” pharmacy so there was no record of this medication at the pharmacy where most of the prescriptions were typically filled. Omeprazole, aspirin, and calcium carbonate are over-the-counter drugs which are not always included in patients’ health records. This can be problematic since each of these medications has potential interactions with other medications.

Pharmacies do not always have clear instructions or indications for all medications a patient is using. Insulin and warfarin directions were only listed as “use as directed”. Pharmacists cannot accurately counsel a patient (or contact a physician with questions about appropriateness of a medication) without knowing the indication (e.g. metoprolol has many uses).

The physician’s office had failed to give the patient specific instructions for selecting an over-the-counter medication. The patient was not provided with adequate information about which calcium tablets she should take. (No instructions were provided about dose, salt form, etc. The patient’s choice of a carbonate salt – along with use of omeprazole—will negate benefits of the calcium since calcium carbonate can only be absorbed in acidic conditions.)

ICS: Levothyroxine. This is used to boost your low thyroid levels. It is usually taken in the morning. It is important to take this medicine on an empty stomach and you must avoid taking it at the same time as certain other medications. For example, you should not take this within 4 hours of taking calcium tablets.

Metoprolol. This medication is used to treat many different problems including irregular heartbeats, high blood pressure, and heart failure. We will need some additional information from your doctor to help you understand why this medication has been prescribed and to make sure that it is the best medication for you. This medication will slow your heart rate and may make you feel fatigued or make it difficult for you to exercise.

Furosemide. This is a “water pill”. It will help you get rid of excess water. The medication will cause you to urinate more often, so it is usually taken in the morning so that you do not awaken many times during the night to use the bathroom. We will need some additional information from your doctor to help you understand why this medication has been prescribed and to make sure that it is the best medication for you. This medication can lower your potassium levels. Your doctor will be checking your potassium levels periodically by a routine blood test. Some people need to take a potassium supplement along with this medication. If you notice an irregular heartbeat, it could be a sign that your potassium levels are too low and you should tell your doctor right away.

Warfarin. This medication is often referred to as a “blood thinner”. You need to have your “bleeding times” checked weekly until they are stable and monthly thereafter. Any time you start taking a new drug or stop taking a medication, you should have your bleeding times checked again. Please tell your doctor immediately if you notice bruising, blood in your stool, a bloody nose, or notice that your gums are bleeding when you brush your teeth. Since this medication is affected by many different foods, you should avoid making any dramatic changes to your diet. It is probably best to shave with an electric razor to minimize the risk of cutting yourself.

Lantus. This is a type of insulin that is very long-acting. It is usually used once daily at night time and provides long-lasting control of your blood sugar. If your blood sugar falls too low you may start to feel hungry or even nauseous like you want to vomit. You could also feel nervous or jittery. You may sweat or your skin might turn cold and clammy. You may begin to feel short-tempered, nervous, afraid, or confused. Your vision may blur. You could also feel unsteady or have trouble walking. Another symptom of low blood sugar is a rapid heartbeat, but you will not notice this since you are also taking metoprolol and that drug slows your heart rate. If you experience low blood sugar, you should eat 15 grams of glucose (tablets, candy bar, glass of milk) right away and check your blood sugar.
Aspirin. The low dose that was prescribed for you is intended to prevent blood clots. You should try to take the drug with food so it does not irritate your stomach.

Alendronate. This medication is used to treat your weakened bones. Your doctor has prescribed it to be taken just once a week. You should take it on an empty stomach, first thing in the morning, before you take any other medications, food, or drinks. You should swallow the tablet with water and stay in an up-right position for 30 minutes. This helps to prevent the medication from irritating the inside of your throat or causing ulcers. This medication should be separated from your calcium supplements by at least 2 hours.

Calcium carbonate + Vitamin D. Combining vitamin D with calcium is always good, since vitamin D helps calcium be absorbed better. Calcium is available in several different forms. The carbonate form requires an acidic environment to be absorbed. However, you are taking omeprazole, which blocks your stomach from producing acid; therefore, omeprazole will prevent the calcium carbonate from working properly to build stronger bones. It would be better for you to take calcium citrate tablets because calcium citrate does not need an acidic environment for absorption. Be sure that you separate your calcium and levothyroxine (thyroid pill) by at least 4 hours so that your thyroid supplement will be absorbed and separate your calcium and your alendronate by at least 2 hours.

Vytorin 10/40 mg. This medication contains 2 different ingredients to help lower your cholesterol. One of the ingredients may have been contributing to your muscle aches due to duplication with the simvastatin tablets (generic Zocor) you were also taking. Since you experienced some muscle aches, the doctor may wish to check some blood work before you continue taking this. If you ever develop pain in your upper abdomen, notice that your urine looks brown in color, or find that your skin or eyes look yellow, you should contact your doctor immediately – as this could indicate a problem with your liver – but this is rare. You should avoid eating or drinking grapefruit products while taking this mediation since the grapefruit can increase the drug levels in your body substantially, placing you at risk of serious muscle problems.
Simvastatin 20 mg. Your doctor intended for you to stop this medication when he gave you samples of Vytorin. Simvastatin is one of the ingredients in Vytorin.

Lovaza. This is another medication used to lower a specific type of cholesterol. It may also prevent blood clots, but this can also increase your risk of bleeding especially since you are taking warfarin. This medication is a good example of why it is important to have your bleeding times checked any time a new medication is started or stopped while you are taking warfarin. Sometimes, this medication causes people to burp or experience a “fishy” after-taste.

Omeprazole. This medication prevents stomach acid from being made. It is often used to treat ulcers, reflux, or heart burn conditions. It is best to take this medication on a short-term basis or use it only intermittently; chronic use can prevent you from being able to appropriately absorb calcium, iron, or magnesium and can also increase your risk of certain types of infections.

Latanoprost 0.05%. This medication lowers the pressure behind your eye and is used to treat glaucoma. When pressure in your eye is too high for long periods of time, it can lead to blindness. Your prescription indicates that you are to put one drop in your left eye only, because only your left eye has elevated pressure. However, we will talk to your eye doctor about this because the drug is known to cause the pupil of your eye to darken in color and make your eye lashes thicker. Most times, patients put drops in both eyes, even if pressure is only elevated in one eye because then the color/lash changes occur uniformly in both eyes. It is best if you keep this medication refrigerated until you use it. Once you open it, it may be stored at room temperature for up to 6 weeks.
